chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When you enter the city, perform ghusl before entering it or when you enter it, then go to the grave of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and send greetings upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).

Then stand at the forward pillar on the right side of the grave, at the head of the grave, facing the qibla, with your left shoulder towards the grave and your right shoulder towards what faces the pulpit, for that is the place of the head of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).

And say: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, alone, without partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. And I bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah, and that you are Muhammad ibn Abdillah. And I bear witness that you conveyed the messages of your Lord, were sincere to your ummah, strove in the path of Allah, and worshipped Allah until certainty came to you with wisdom and good admonition, and you fulfilled what was upon you of the truth, and that you were gentle with the believers and firm with the disbelievers.
So Allah brought you to the highest honor of the station of the honored.
Praise is to Allah who saved us through you from polytheism and misguidance.

O Allah, so make Your prayer, and the prayer of Your neared angels, and Your righteous servants, and Your sent prophets, and the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth, and whoever glorified You, O Lord of the worlds, from the first and the last, upon Muhammad, Your servant and Messenger and Prophet and Trustworthy and Noble and Beloved and Special and Chosen and Purest and Best of Your creation.
O Allah, grant him the rank and give him the proximity from Paradise, and raise him to a Praised Station with which the first and the last will envy him.

O Allah, indeed You said: 'And if they, when they wronged themselves, had come to You and asked forgiveness of Allah and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them, they would have found Allah to be Accepting of Repentance, Merciful.'
And I have come to you seeking forgiveness, repenting from my sins, and I turn to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, my Lord and your Lord, through you, that He may forgive my sins.

And if you have a need, place the grave of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) behind your shoulder, face the qibla, raise your hands, and ask for your need, for it is more likely to be granted, if Allah wills.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended ritual and supplication for visiting the Prophet's grave in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the canonical etiquette for Ziyarat al-Nabi, emphasizing ritual purity and the specific orientation of standing at the head of the grave (where the Prophet's head rests) facing the Qibla. It highlights the Shia theological concept of *tawassul* (seeking intercession), where the Prophet serves as a spiritual conduit to Allah, supported by the recitation of Surah Al Imran 3:135 to frame the supplicant's repentance.
